outgoing.explanation: The Hotten and ROLLCO negative searches extend the online/source-coverage map beyond the earlier infrastructure negatives and show why the remaining origin state is still a bounded negative rather than an unsearched gap.

The newly assimilated emigrant-list and livery-register negatives narrow the open research program by resolving part of the prior emigrant/trade residual without producing a positive identity or route.

The London port-emigration and livery-company negatives bound the trade-training conclusion: they add no enrolled John Gurney apprenticeship or passenger record, so the informal/country-training reading remains a bounded inference rather than proof of where or how he trained.

Hotten and the underlying port-list pathway add another negative passenger-list check, reinforcing that the passenger silence is expected record survival rather than evidence against migration in the 1638-early-1641 window.

statement: The London port-emigration lists and the livery-company registers, searched for John Gurney's crossing and trade, return no emigrant John Gurney. Hotten's Original Lists (behind them TNA E 157/20) hold no Gurney passenger in any spelling; a ROLLCO all-company livery sweep finds no East-Anglian Gurney apprentice, the sole provincial tailoring-Gurney being the eliminated Buckinghamshire Candidate-A family.
